items.headline: Press secretary Katie Zacharia out after less than a week
items.summary: The White House says Katie Zacharia is transitioning out of the press secretary job, days after her first official day on Monday. Trump had said she was asked to reconsider the role after a turbulent start.

items.headline: Police: Oregon shooter targeted special education classroom
items.summary: Police in Bend, Oregon, say the 16-year-old shooter attacked a special education classroom before he was killed, and that four people died. The man who stopped the attack has two daughters at the school, his mother says.

items.headline: Settlers attack West Bank olive harvest, beat U.S. photojournalist
items.summary: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages during the olive harvest in the occupied West Bank, burning cars and trees. Several people were injured, including a Washington Post photographer.

items.headline: Carney says U.S. is trying to 'break' Canada before Alberta vote
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney told a pro-Canada rally in Calgary that outside forces are trying to break up the country as Alberta votes on a separation path. The warning followed President Trump's renewed talk of Canada as a '51st state.'

items.headline: Wind-driven fire burns coastal homes in Southern California
items.summary: High winds are fueling a fast-moving Southern California fire that has burned homes along the coast. Thousands of people have been told to evacuate.

items.headline: DOJ warns California officials over noncitizen ballots
items.summary: The Justice Department says California election officials who process ballots from suspected noncitizen voters could face criminal investigation. The warning comes ahead of the November midterms.

items.headline: China moves to curb exports of AI and other technology
items.summary: China says it will restrict exports of some technologies, including artificial intelligence, citing national security risks. The move comes as Beijing and Washington pursue talks on AI safety.

items.headline: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
items.summary: Chatbot startup Character.AI, which drew millions of users, is filing for bankruptcy after Google hired its founders and licensed its technology. NPR's Planet Money looks at what the case says about AI startups.

items.headline: Nature fundraising falls short before UN biodiversity summit
items.summary: Efforts to raise money to protect oceans, forests, rivers and other key natural areas have fallen short of targets. The shortfall comes ahead of a major UN biodiversity summit.

items.headline: Report says Trump's drug-stock holdings grew sharply
items.summary: A congressional Democratic report says Trump's pharmaceutical stock holdings rose from up to $1.7 million in 2024 to as much as $56.2 million by the end of 2025. Democrats say some of the companies received Medicare exemptions.

digest.overview:
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving the job less than a week after her first day, the White House said Friday. President Trump issued an executive order implementing a new Russia and Iran sanctions law while waiving many of its measures. Police in Bend, Oregon, said the 16-year-old school shooter attacked a special education classroom before a parent stopped him. The Justice Department warned California election officials that processing ballots from suspected noncitizens could bring prosecution. The Bryson Fire near Malibu grew to about 200 acres, burning coastal homes and forcing evacuations. A congressional Democratic report said Trump's drug-stock holdings rose to as much as $56.2 million. No Kings organizers are turning this weekend's protests toward voter turnout.

Abroad, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians during the West Bank olive harvest and beat a Washington Post photographer. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic remains about 70% below pre-war levels. Vladimir Putin said a border security zone is not up for negotiation with Kyiv, and Belgium pledged 10 F-16s to Ukraine this year. China said it will curb exports of AI and other technology on security grounds. Canada's Mark Carney warned that outside forces want to break up the country ahead of Monday's Alberta referendum. A poll showed Israel's governing bloc and the Jewish opposition tied at 51 seats each before the Oct. 27 election. Hurricane Trudy strengthened to Category 3 off Mexico's Pacific coast, and fundraising to protect key natural sites fell short ahead of a UN biodiversity summit.

home.overview:
Baseball got a rain check: heavy rain in Cleveland postponed ALCS Game 4, so the Guardians, up 2–1 on the Rays, resume the series Saturday at 8 p.m. ET with Game 5 on Sunday, while the Brewers wait for the World Series starting Oct. 23. Shohei Ohtani says he plans to pitch again in 2027. In the NFL, Lamar Jackson and Jalen Hurts are out for Week 6, the Eagles are adding Joe Milton, and Caleb Williams says he is ready to face Atlanta. Sunday brings Texans-Jaguars in London, Chargers at Chiefs with Patrick Mahomes off the injury report, and Cowboys at Packers. NBA rosters are being trimmed before Tuesday's opening night.

Wolves won 2–1 at Burnley to jump into the Championship top six, Frankfurt edged Köln 1–0 and Toulouse won 3–0 at Le Mans. Saturday's Premier League slate has Everton vs Chelsea, Man City vs Ipswich and Liverpool at Brentford, with Barcelona at Real Betis and Bayern vs RB Leipzig also on the card. In Korea, Ulsan HD beat Bucheon 2–1, and Suwon FC's stoppage-time winner at Seongnam pulled them within two points of K League 2 leaders Suwon Samsung. In the KBO, Kim Do-yeong homered twice as Kia beat LG 5–1 to open the first round.

brief: Kim Do-yeong hit two home runs and drove in four as Kia beat LG 5–1 in Game 1 of their best-of-five first-round series in Gwangju.
Kia starter James Naile allowed one run over seven innings with six strikeouts, and Jeon Sang-hyun earned his first postseason save.
LG's Song Chan-eui homered in the second inning, but Anders Tolhurst gave up two homers and took the loss.
The sold-out crowd of 18,900 extended the KBO's postseason sellout streak, and Game 2 is Sunday at 2 p.m. KST in Gwangju.
The series moves to Jamsil for Games 3 and 4 on Oct. 20–21, with the winner facing No. 2 Samsung.
